issues.failure_explanation: The introduction claims that the paper extends Chernoff's product formula to bi-continuous semigroups arising from nonlinear flows and proves well-posedness and contraction of the splitting operators. In reality, Theorem 4.1 (CPFBi) is quoted directly from F. Kühnemund's 2001 dissertation [3] with the proof simply given as 'See [3]', and no proof of well-posedness or contraction of the splitting operators is provided.

failure_location.quote: \textit{Bi-continuous Chernoff extension}. We extend Chernoff's product formula to bicontinuous semigroups on bounded continuous functions arising from nonlinear flows, proving well-posedness and contraction of the splitting operators (Theorem \ref{CPFBi}).

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Clarify in the introduction that Chernoff's bi-continuous product formula is recalled from Kühnemund [3] and applied to Koopman semigroups, removing the claim of proving the extension.
issues.overall_effect: The second advertised main contribution in the introduction is unsupported by the mathematical content of the paper.
issues.title: Unsubstantiated claim of extending and proving Chernoff product formula for bi-continuous semigroups
issues.why_classification: Correcting the attribution and scope of the prose claim requires only a minor textual adjustment and leaves all actual mathematical results unaffected.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
\begin{remark} Since the proof of Theorem \ref{ha} given  in \cite{JD5} is of an algebraic nature, it can be extended to bi-continuous contraction semigroups without changing any of arguments. 
  \end{remark}

issues.failure_explanation: Theorem 4.2 (ha) explicitly requires the semigroups to be analytic contraction semigroups when the splitting coefficients are complex. All higher-order methods presented in the paper (order p >= 3, such as Proposition 4.3 and Theorems 4.3, 4.4, 4.5) use complex coefficients. However, Koopman-Lie semigroups induced by ODE flows on C_b(\Omega) are translation/flow groups, which are never analytic. Consequently, the operators e^{\alpha t \mathcal{K}_i} for non-real \alpha are not defined as bounded operators on C_b(\Omega) (evaluation at complex times would require analytic continuation of C_b functions), violating the required hypothesis of Theorem 4.2 and invalidating the claimed operator error bounds.

failure_location.quote:
\begin{theorem}{\cite{JD5}, \cite{JD6}}.\label{ha}
Let $\mathcal{K}_{1}$, $\mathcal{K}_{2}$, and $\mathcal{K}=\mathcal{K}_{1}$+$\mathcal{K}_{2}$ be generators of strongly continuous contraction semigroups on a Banach space $X$ (or analytic contraction semigroups if the coefficients $\alpha_{j}$'s and $\beta_{j}$'s are complex).

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must restrict the function space and vector fields to entire/holomorphic systems where complex flows exist and generate sectorial semigroups, or replace the complex-coefficient schemes with real-coefficient splittings.
issues.overall_effect: The theoretical error bounds and convergence guarantees for all splitting schemes of order p >= 3 applied to Koopman-Lie semigroups fail.
issues.title: Violation of analyticity hypothesis when applying complex-coefficient splitting bounds to Koopman semigroups
issues.why_classification: Resolving this requires changing the entire analytical framework from C_b(\Omega) to spaces of holomorphic functions and abandoning or replacing the central high-order complex-time splitting architecture.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: \STATE \textbf{Input:} Let \( x \) be the number of exponential terms for \( N = 2 \)

issues.failure_explanation: Algorithm 1 accepts the number of exponential terms for N=2, denoted by x. For the Lie-Trotter splitting, x = 2. Line 2 initializes List1 with [(x-1)/2, (x+1)/2], which for x=2 results in non-integers [0.5, 1.5]. Subsequent multiplications produce fractional values (e.g. Total number of terms = 2.5 for N=3, instead of 3), because the algorithm implicitly assumes x is odd (as in symmetric splittings).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State in the input preconditions that x must be odd, or add a special case for x=2 returning N terms.
issues.overall_effect: Algorithm 1 fails to compute the correct term counts for the Lie-Trotter splitting, which is one of the methods tabulated in Table 1.
issues.title: Algorithm 1 is ill-defined and fails for even input x (Lie-Trotter splitting)
issues.why_classification: A minor local condition or branch on x=2 completely fixes the procedure without altering any other mathematical result.
